slides.title: Systematically Monitoring the Public Scientific Conversation
bullets: Tracks conversations across professional networks, forums, publication comments, congress hashtags
Aims to spot trends, concerns, knowledge gaps and opinion patterns
Adapted from social listening to health's ethical and rigor standards

slides.title: Broader and More Continuous Than Competitive Intelligence
bullets: Competitive intelligence focuses narrowly on one congress
Medical listening runs continuously, all year round
Its scope covers the whole conversation on a disease or area
Interested in the topic, not only in what competitors say

slides.title: Three Sources of Signal
bullets: What content drives the most discussion among HCPs online
Hashtags and mentions tracked around relevant congresses
Forums and communities where professionals speak more informally
Informal spaces often surface more honest doubts and frustrations

slides.title: Feeding Real Gaps Back Into the Plan
bullets: Feeds the evidence gap inventory in the Medical Plan
Informs content journeys built on real, not assumed, questions
Helps surface emerging DOLs before traditional mapping catches them

slides.title: Public, Contextual, and Formally Channeled
bullets: Limit sources to public and open conversations only
Respect the privacy and context of what you observe
Never identify a professional from an informal conversation without consent
Route findings through formal insight processes, not casual mentions

slides.title: A Wider View Than Your Own Conversations Alone
bullets: Amplifies insight-gathering beyond direct personal interactions
Offers a panoramic read of what the community cares about right now

takeaway.title: Medical listening turns the public scientific conversation into structured, ethical insight
bullets: It runs year-round and covers the full conversation, not just competitors
LinkedIn, congress hashtags and clinical forums each add a different signal
Findings must stay public-source, contextual and formally documented
